question: Our CI wrapper runs `npx doc-detective runTests -i docs -e --logLevel info > dd.log` and then fails the build with `grep -E "Element not found within timeout|Failed Items" dd.log`. Since the runner picked up Doc Detective 5, the log shows "Warning: `--exit-on-fail` is deprecated. It's now the default, so remove it." and "Warning: `--logLevel` is deprecated. Rename it to `--log-level`.", and the grep never matches, even on runs where I can see a `find` step failed. Did v5 drop those flags? How should the wrapper detect failures now?

facts.text: The deprecated spellings still work and only warn: `-e`/`--exit-on-fail` can be removed because failing the run is now the default, `--logLevel` becomes `--log-level`, and `runTests` becomes `run` (or no command).

The grep stops matching because v5 rewrote the messages and summary: a failed find reads ``Couldn't find element `...`.`` or ``Couldn't find an element within `timeout` (5000 ms).``, and the summary lists `Failed (N):` instead of `Failed Items:`. Logs also moved to stderr, so `> dd.log` doesn't capture them.

Use the exit code instead of matching text: `0` means no test failed, `1` means at least one test failed, and `2` means nothing valid was tested. For details, read `result` and `resultCode` from the results (`--output <file>` or `--json`).

must_not: v5 removed `--logLevel`, `-e`/`--exit-on-fail`, or `runTests`, so they error or are ignored.
Doc Detective still exits 0 when tests fail unless you pass `-e` or `--exit-on-fail`.
Update the grep to match the new message text.

wrong.why: says the flags were removed and keeps grepping
wrong.answer:
v5 removed `--logLevel` and `-e`, so they're ignored now, and the run exits 0 even when a test fails. Switch the grep to the new wording:

```bash
npx doc-detective run -i docs --log-level info > dd.log
grep -E "Couldn't find|Failed \(" dd.log
```

replace.from: npx doc-detective run --input docs --log-level info --output results.json
replace.to: npx doc-detective run --input docs --log-level info --results-file results.json

replace.from: Let the exit code decide instead: `0` means no test failed and at least one passed or warned, `1` means at least one test failed, and `2` means nothing valid was tested, such as an invalid spec or a run where every test skipped.
